From video input to XR display

Video from the endoscopy equipment passes through a capture card into the custom Mac app. Two capture inputs are synchronized by timestamp and combined into SBS. Single SBS and 2D inputs are encoded without a separate stereo compositing step. The XR app decodes and displays the video received over WebRTC.

STORZ direct USB connection ↗

Dual-input frame synchronization and SBS compositing

The Mac receives one eye view from each of two CV-190 units and combines them into one SBS frame. SBS (side-by-side) places the left and right views next to each other within a single frame.

Dual capture
Two capture cards are assigned to the left- and right-eye inputs. Frames arrive independently from each card.
Frame synchronization
Left and right frames with nearby capture timestamps are selected for compositing.
SBS compositing
The two views are placed side by side at the configured size. In the October 29 CV-190 test, two 1920×1080 inputs were combined into a 3840×1080 frame.
CV-190 video outputs and capture setup ↗

Single-input SBS and 2D video

The OTV-S300 and OTV-S700 supplied an SBS frame containing both eye views. The STORZ test setup supplied a 2D frame. Each used a single capture input.

The processor’s left/right layout is retained. The frame goes to encoding and streaming without synchronizing or combining two separate inputs.

2D input

2D frame

A single image is streamed without stereo compositing. XR displays it in a 2D video window.

A 1920×1080 Half SBS input contains a 960×1080 region for each eye. Upscaling at the send stage does not add detail to that input.

From encoding to XR display

The Mac app’s streaming resolution, target frame rate and bitrate were adjusted to reduce live-streaming latency. Video is compressed with a codec suited to the receiving device and sent over WebRTC. The XR app decodes and displays it.

SBS
The left region is shown to the left eye and the right region to the right eye.
2D
The frame is displayed as one image, without stereo separation.

CV-190 testing started with downscaled live streaming, then progressed to settings that retained Full HD per eye. The Full HD article documents those settings and measurements from the receive logs.
